data.narrative:
Lightmatter is a Series C semiconductor company that has raised $420M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Tenstorrent, d-Matrix, Positron AI, DEEPX) spanning valuations from $529M to $2.7B, alongside 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) with a median price-to-sales multiple of 21.0x.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a typical 1.7x step-up multiplier from Series C to the next funding stage, using the $420M raised as a proxy base, implying $714M. Peer-median analysis across the 4 private comparables yields a median valuation of $1.5B, with a range of $529M to $2.7B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot be applied due to absence of revenue disclosure for the private target.

The two applicable methods yield a triangulated valuation range of $607M to $1.7B, with a median point of $1.1B. The 1.7x spread reflects material dispersion in peer stage and maturity within the semiconductor frontier-tech cohort. Key uncertainties include Lightmatter's actual revenue trajectory relative to peers, capital efficiency post-Series C, and whether the company's optical-computing differentiation commands a premium or discount to traditional semiconductor valuations.
